cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Steer the Suspicion
cards.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Your shelf fell because they supplied the wrong bracket.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You fitted it upside down. Look at the arrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. That's a misleading arrow. We should photograph it for the manufacturer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You drew that arrow. I watched you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because theirs was missing. Put that in the complaint; they made us supply our own safety markings.

mechanism: A dictates complaint evidence so even A's own misleading mark becomes the manufacturer's responsibility.
confusable: Unlike blaming a defect once, A must redirect each correction that brings the installation failure back to A.
comparison: A self-drawn bracket arrow differs from a leaking pen and delivery claim.
seedUse: The seed's photograph and complaint instructions already let S01 command the interpretation as D133 redirects blame.
